_comment: EntityOS service registry for neural_immune on frank-api (systemctl SYSTEM scope, not --user). policy=restart: circuit-breaker-guarded auto-restart allowed. policy=observe: NEVER restarted automatically, only logged/tracked (for oneshot jobs that are normally inactive between timer runs, and for clayverse-verdichtung which is intentionally idle most of the time). Adjust here, not in code -- collector.py loads this file at startup (env IMMUNE_SERVICES_CONFIG overrides the path).

clayverse-kern.note: ClayVerse-Kern -- Schicht zwischen Oberflaeche und Claude Code. Must stay running.

clayverse-wikiarbeit.note: Dauerarbeit an der Wissensbasis, Type=simple/Restart=always -- meant to run continuously, so critical=true (an 'inactive' reading here IS a real outage, not idle-by-design). Chosen as the unkritische SELF-HEALING TEST TARGET precisely because losing it briefly does not hurt EntityOS's user-facing function -- unlike clayverse-kern/puls/eos-publish.

eos-publish.note: Zeros einziger Weg nach draussen. Must stay running.

clayverse-verdichtung.note: Intentionally idle most of the time -- only works past a threshold. Do NOT restart on 'inactive'.

eos-systeme.note: Oneshot via timer, alle 15s -- very frequent, expect it inactive most snapshots.

docker_container.name: entityos
docker_container.note: Docker RestartPolicy=unless-stopped already self-heals this. neural_immune only logs health via 'docker inspect', never restarts it (out of scope: could interrupt entityos.frank.ink).

warm_pool.note: Not a systemd unit -- plain 'claude -p' CLI processes. neural_immune only counts and logs, never restarts (spawning is the warm-pool manager's job, not the immune system's).
